entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Domenico Maria Novara da Ferrara (1454–1504) was an Italian scientist and engineer who contributed significantly to the field of mathematics and astronomy during the Renaissance. He worked at the court of Ferrara, producing several treatises on geometry and optics, including his magnum opus, the 'Trattato della prospettiva' (Treatise on Perspective).

Novara's work had a profound impact on the development of Renaissance art and architecture, influencing artists such as Leonardo da Vinci and Michelangelo. His treatise on perspective, in particular, revolutionized the way artists understood and represented space in their works.

Despite his significant contributions to the scientific community, Novara's legacy was largely forgotten until the 20th century, when his work was rediscovered and reevaluated by historians and scholars.

As a testament to his enduring influence, Novara's treatise on perspective remains a foundational text in the study of art and architecture, and his work continues to inspire artists and scholars to this day.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Novara's work on perspective had a significant impact on the development of Renaissance art, influencing artists such as Leonardo da Vinci and Michelangelo. His treatise on perspective remains a foundational text in the study of art and architecture, shaping the way artists understood and represented space in their works.
